newsitem.title: UK: AMA named as UK GSA for Arrow Air.
newsitem.headline: AMA named as UK GSA for Arrow Air.

text.p: Miami-based freighter operator Arrow Air has named Air Marketing Associates (AMA) as its first UK general sales agent, the latter said in a statement.
It added that it will handle UK sales of Arrow's scheduled services from its main hub at Miami, to six key points throughout Central and South America.
The destinations are Lima, Quito, Guayaquil, Asuncion, Ciudad del Este and San Juan.
Arrow begins services to Panama City this month, and is studying the addition of Caracas, Buenos Aires, Iquitos, Montevideo and Santiago de Chile to its schedule, the statement said.

Capacity to the U.S. will be provided by UK Leisure's Boeing 767 aircraft which operate daily during the summer, an interline arrangement already used by AMA to link with its client carriers whose services fly out of Miami, it added.
The UK GSA will help Arrow in marketing east-bound cargo to Europe through its recently-opened Miami-based subsidiary AMA Inc.
This will seek to generate traffic via the UK where AMA will handle transhipment onto Aeroflot, CSA Balkan Bulgarian, LOT and Transaero services to Eastern Europe and the CIS.
Major east-bound commodities are expected to be pharmaceuticals. cut flowers and fresh fruit.

Len Bunn, AMA's Group Managing Director, said:" Arrow is investing heavily in new equipment which will increase its capacity. The potential for traffic over London - both west-bound and east-bound is vast...we have a number of plans for new products to be launched in partnership with Arrow in the coming months," .

Arrow Air operates a fleet of six Douglas DC8-62F, DC8-63F and three Lockheed L-1O11-200F freighters. The latter are progressively replacing the older narrow-bodied aircraft providing greater capacity, improved reliability and greater operational flexibility through quieter (stage III)noise compliance.

The airline is also expected to benefit from stricter U.S. regulations on the carriage of hazardous goods on passenger aircraft, and staff have undergone extensive training to prepare for an anticipated boom in such traffic, the statement added.

Arrow provides a mix of scheduled and ad hoc capacity, and is boosting traffic via Miami with the 1996 start of express road feeder services to and from Atlanta, Houston, Dallas Fort Worth, Orlando, Tampa and New Orleans.

Plans are under way to form alliances with other domestic and international carriers in order to extend its network, the statement added but did not give other details. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax:5017
